name: A Molecular Mechanism
description: Fig 6b/6c — a molecular mechanism as a process with typed physical channels. Fig 6b: the molecular interface exchanges matter (chemical, mol·s⁻¹), charge (electrical, C·s⁻¹/A), rotary work / torque (mechanical, N·m), and energy (thermal, J·s⁻¹/W), and is defined over molecular structure (PDB/SMILES) — no cell-level boundary. Fig 6c: the chemical channel refines into specialized subports — substrates, cofactors, catalysts, products. The mechanism is wired to a `ports` store (the typed channels + structure) and a `subports` store (the chemical refinement). draft process: unit-bearing ports + behavior contract, no update dynamics.

contract.summary: F₁Fₒ ATP synthase — a four-channel molecular transducer
contract.description: A molecular mechanism as a process with typed physical channels, defined over molecular structure (PDB/SMILES) with no cell-level boundary. The F₁Fₒ ATP synthase couples a transmembrane proton flux to rotary torque and ATP synthesis, conserving matter, charge, angular momentum (rotary work), and energy across its four channels. The chemical channel refines into substrates, cofactors, catalysts, and products.

symbols.R, T, F: gas constant, absolute temperature, Faraday constant
symbols.e: elementary charge (per-molecule torque uses e, not F)
symbols.n_turn: protons translocated per full rotation (c-ring stoichiometry, ≈ 10)
symbols.\u0394G_ATP: Gibbs free energy of ATP synthesis (J·mol⁻¹)
